text: Which of the following statements about atoms, molecules and ions is correct? I. An anion is a positively charged ion II. Isotopes are atoms of the same element with different mass numbers III. Isotopes have the same mass number but different atomic numbers
explanation:
Isotopes are atoms of the same element with different mass numbers — this is correct.

The other two statements are not true: "An anion is a positively charged ion" and "Isotopes have the same mass number but different atomic numbers" both misstate the physics.

So only II is correct.

text: An element has two isotopes of mass numbers 26 and 28 with relative abundances 10% and 90% respectively. Calculate its relative atomic mass.
Two atoms have atomic number 16 but mass numbers 24 and 28 respectively. What is the relationship between them?
options: They have different numbers of both protons and neutrons
They have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons
They have the same mass number but different atomic numbers
They have the same number of neutrons but different numbers of protons
explanation:

Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons are isotopes.

text: An atom has mass number 16 and atomic number 10. How many neutrons does it contain?
explanation:
The atomic number gives the number of protons, and in a neutral atom the number of electrons equals the number of protons.

Number of neutrons = mass number − atomic number = \(16 - 10 = 6\)

So the number of neutrons is 6.
